port-lincoln-1.name: Whalers Way
port-lincoln-1.bio: A 15 km drive on private land south of Port Lincoln past cliffs, blowholes, caves and beaches; a permit is needed to enter.

notes.pin: Wikivoyage: drive starts 20 km south of Port Lincoln; gate/permit point and Red Banks beach are visitor points. Use the drive midpoint.
notes.cost: Permit $40 per car, date-limited, includes 1 night free camping (portlincoln.com.au, sold by Port Lincoln Visitor Information Centre). Red Banks road 4WD only at time of reading. No Wikipedia article titled Whalers Way, so wiki omitted.

port-lincoln-2.name: Axel Stenross Maritime Museum
port-lincoln-2.bio: Boatbuilding museum on Port Lincoln's foreshore with a Finnish carpenter's original workshops and a working slipway.

notes.cost: Adult $10, seniors $8 (eyrepeninsula.com listing). Open Tue, Thu, Sun 9.30-4.30, Sat and public holidays 1-4.30 (not stored).

port-lincoln-3.name: Winter Hill Lookout
port-lincoln-3.bio: A lookout above Port Lincoln with views over Boston Bay, Lincoln National Park and Spencer Gulf.
port-lincoln-3.ticket_note: Council-run open lookout; no single operator site.

notes.pin: Winter Hill Drive, Port Lincoln: lookout/car park on the hill (OSM tourism=viewpoint).

port-lincoln-4.name: Port Lincoln Old Mill
port-lincoln-4.bio: The 1846 Old Mill, Port Lincoln's oldest standing structure, now a lookout tower over Boston Bay with a rose garden.
port-lincoln-4.ticket_note: Open reserve; no operator site found.

notes.cost: Free per listing; steep steps to the top.

port-lincoln-5.name: Makybe Diva Statue
port-lincoln-5.bio: Bronze statue of Makybe Diva, the first horse to win three consecutive Melbourne Cups, on Port Lincoln's foreshore.

port-lincoln-6.name: Port Lincoln Street Art Trail
port-lincoln-6.bio: A self-guided walk past murals of marine life and local history in Port Lincoln's streets and laneways.

notes.pin: Walk route in the town centre; use the trail page's mural map midpoint, not a single mural.

port-lincoln-7.name: Parnkalla Trail
port-lincoln-7.bio: A coastal walking and cycling trail from Port Lincoln along Boston Bay towards Lincoln National Park.
port-lincoln-7.ticket_note: Council trail; no operator site verified.

notes.pin: Linear route: midpoint of the OSM route; trail starts in Port Lincoln.

port-lincoln-8.name: Fishery Bay
port-lincoln-8.bio: A surf beach and surfing reserve on Right Whale Road, with remains of an old whaling station nearby.
port-lincoln-8.ticket_note: Open beach; no single steward site verified.

notes.pin: Fishery Bay Surfing Reserve, Right Whale Road, Sleaford; use the car park/lookout.
notes.wiki: Wikipedia title Fishery Bay redirects to Sleaford Bay, a broader article, so wiki omitted (draft wiki dropped). Wikipedia has Fishery Bay Surfing Reserve (title unconfirmed as this place).
notes.cost: Free per listing; whaling station remains per draft source, not re-verified.

port-lincoln-9.name: Mikkira Station
port-lincoln-9.bio: A working sheep station west of Port Lincoln with a sanctuary for wild koalas, visited on guided koala safaris.

notes.pin: Provisional point is the Wikipedia locality Mikkira; station visitor point to be checked.
notes.cost: Tour South koala safari "from $159" (eyrepeninsula.com listing); price not confirmed on operator site. Draft claim of permit and gate key not found in sources, removed.

lincoln-national-park-1.name: Memory Cove
lincoln-national-park-1.bio: A secluded white-sand bay inside Lincoln National Park, reached by booking a vehicle entry and collecting a gate key.

notes.pin: Wikipedia point provisional; use the lookout/beach car park inside the Wilderness Protection Area.
notes.cost: Vehicle entry $14.40 per vehicle (parks.sa.gov.au Memory Cove page); access limited to 15 vehicles a day (eyrepeninsula.com). Wiki title Memory Cove not confirmed.

lincoln-national-park-2.name: Stamford Hill
lincoln-national-park-2.bio: A 1.6 km return walk up to the Flinders monument, with views over Port Lincoln and its beaches.

notes.pin: Summit monument (OSM historic=memorial / peak); trailhead car park at foot.
notes.cost: Free assumed: the NPWS Lincoln page does not list it, Wikivoyage lists it as a walk. Unverified whether it is inside the park entry fee area.

destination.name: Port Lincoln
destination.tagline: Seafood capital on Boston Bay, with shark cage diving and wild coast
destination.description: Port Lincoln sits on Boston Bay at the southern tip of the Eyre Peninsula and is known as Australia's seafood capital. Tuna and other seafood come off the working harbour, and boats leave from here for great white shark cage diving. Lookouts, a murals trail and a maritime museum fill a day in town, and Lincoln National Park and Whalers Way lie a short drive south.

goodToKnow.title: Whalers Way needs a permit
goodToKnow.detail: Whalers Way is private land. Buy a permit before you enter, from the visitor centre or online, and expect unsealed roads.

goodToKnow.title: Book shark dives ahead
goodToKnow.detail: Cage diving trips leave from the town harbour and sell out in peak season, so book before you arrive.

goodToKnow.title: Distances are long
goodToKnow.detail: Adelaide is about 650 km away, so plan a fly-in or an overnight stop on the drive.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} bring mild weather for coastal walks and drives, while summer is hot and busy.

destination.name: Lincoln National Park
destination.tagline: Granite headlands, quiet bays and big dunes south of Port Lincoln
destination.description: Lincoln National Park overlooks Boston Bay on the southern Eyre Peninsula, with granite headlands, sheltered bays and offshore islands. On its southern side the Sleaford-Wanna dunes meet the surf of the Southern Ocean. Visitors walk cliff-top and beach trails, camp by the water and watch for whales in winter, and the secluded Memory Cove is reached by booking a gate key.

goodToKnow.title: Pay entry before you go
goodToKnow.detail: Vehicle entry is charged per vehicle and must be paid before entering the park.

goodToKnow.title: Memory Cove is by booking
goodToKnow.detail: Book vehicle entry for Memory Cove and collect the gate key, as access is limited each day.
